candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is eccrine porocarcinoma, a malignant tumor of eccrine sweat gland ductal epithelium. Squamous cell carcinoma is a separate keratinocyte-derived malignancy. Although both can present as recurrent skin lesions on acral sites with regional nodal metastasis, they are distinct diagnostic entities with different histogenesis, histopathology, and clinical management. The clinical features (recurrence after partial amputation, firm indurated lesion on thumb dorsum, axillary nodal metastasis) are characteristic of eccrine porocarcinoma, not SCC.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Squamous cell carcinoma is a distinct epithelial malignancy; eccrine porocarcinoma is a malignant adnexal tumor of sweat gland origin

case_quality_flags: Classic eccrine porocarcinoma presentation: acral location, recurrence after prior resection, regional lymph node metastasis; diagnosis requires histopathologic confirmation with immunohistochemistry
